title: [aoti] Fix use-after-free in pointer_to_optional_list
body:
`pointer_to_optional_list` returned `std::optional<c10::ArrayRef<T>>` whose `ArrayRef` viewed into a `std::vector<T>` temporary. When the caller's `T` differs from the on-wire `U` (e.g. `T=c10::SymInt`, `U=int64_t`), `pointer_to_list` materializes a fresh `std::vector<T>` by value; that vector is destroyed at the end of `pointer_to_optional_list`, leaving the `ArrayRef` inside the returned optional dangling. The receiving op (e.g. `convolution_backward_symint`) then reads freed `SymInt` memory — caught by ASAN as a heap-use-after-free at `c10::SymInt::is_heap_allocated`. Affects any AOTI op whose generated shim has an optional symint-list parameter.

Wrap the result in a new `OwningOptionalArrayRef<T>` that holds the `std::vector<T>` itself and converts implicitly to both `c10::OptionalArrayRef<T>` and `std::optional<c10::ArrayRef<T>>` (the two parameter shapes the generated shims use). Because the wrapper is the temporary in the call site's full expression, its storage stays alive for the duration of the receiving function call. No regeneration of `c_shim_*.cpp` is needed: both implicit conversions land at parameter types the generator already targets.

Reproduced under an ASAN build of pytorch on ROCm in test/inductor/test_gpu_cpp_wrapper.py::TestGpuWrapper::test_conv_backward_cuda_gpu_wrapper (and the dynamic_shapes variant).

Authored with Claude.
